name: High-grade astrocytoma with piloid features

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of high-grade astrocytic tumor with piloid (hair-like) cellular morphology
Detection of characteristic molecular alterations including MAPK pathway activation and CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion
MRI showing contrast-enhancing mass with infiltrative growth pattern in cerebral hemispheres

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of high-grade astrocytoma with piloid features plus supporting molecular profile
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology and molecular genetics per WHO CNS tumor classification

searchTerms: gradual worsening of localized neurological problems
progressive weakness or numbness in one area
head pain due to increased fluid in brain

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vomiting caused by increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Motor weakness localized to affected brain region
searchTerms: motor loss in affected brain region
loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-specific but may show elevated protein
imaging: MRI with contrast showing heterogeneously enhancing mass with infiltrative margins
genetic: MAPK pathway gene alterations (e.g., BRAF mutations or fusions)
Absence of IDH1/2 mutations typical for other astrocytomas
other: Histopathology showing piloid morphology with high mitotic activity
Immunohistochemistry positive for GFAP and variable p53 expression

distinguishingFeatures: Lower grade tumor with classic biphasic pattern
Lack of high mitotic activity and necrosis
Different molecular profile without CDKN2A/B deletion
IDH wildtype with different molecular markers
Distinct histopathological features including microvascular proliferation

redFlags: New onset seizures in adult without prior history
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021
Orphanet: High-grade astrocytoma with piloid features (ORPHA:715721)
Jones DTW, et al. Molecular characteristics of high-grade astrocytomas with piloid features. Acta Neuropathol. 2020
